chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ibn Abi Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, among the people with the greatest regret on the Day of Judgment is the one who portrayed justice, then opposed it to something else.
ai.seo_question: Who will have the greatest regret on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the gravity of 'self-deception' (ghurur), where individuals convince themselves of their own righteousness while acting contrary to it. It serves as a critical ethical warning against the disconnect between professed values and actual conduct, a theme central to the concept of 'Adl (justice) in Twelver theology. The regret mentioned is not merely for failing to be just, but for the specific hypocrisy of claiming justice while violating it.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one with the greatest of regrets on the Day of Judgment would be the one who portrayed justice, then opposed it to something else’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from ibn abu Ya’fur from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Of the people who, on the Day of Judgment, will regret the most is one who preaches justice but himself does not yield to justice.”
